title: Lead Generation for Small Business and Client Onboarding
description: Lead generation for small business in Australia: get found, capture enquiries, reply fast and onboard clients well. Includes a checklist and automations.
dek: How Australian small businesses can get more leads, reply faster, onboard new clients smoothly and automate the follow-up.

faq.q: What is the best way to generate leads for a small business in Australia?
faq.a: For most local businesses, the best lead source is Google: a complete Business Profile, plenty of recent reviews, and a website built to turn visitors into enquiries. Referrals from happy customers come a close second, and both cost far less than paid ads.

faq.q: How quickly should I respond to a new lead?
faq.a: As fast as you can. Send an automatic reply instantly, and aim for a personal reply within the hour during business hours. People often contact several businesses at once, so the first helpful reply has a real advantage.

faq.q: Is an AI receptionist worth it for a small business?
faq.a: If you regularly miss calls because you're on the tools or with a customer, usually yes. If you rarely miss calls, an instant SMS reply to missed calls may be enough.

Everything that happens between a customer saying yes and their first great experience with you: welcome message, confirmation, preparation, reminders and the first follow-up. Good onboarding cuts no-shows and makes referrals more likely.

faq.q: Do I need a CRM as a small business?
faq.a: You need one place where every lead is stored and tracked. That can start as a spreadsheet. Move to a proper CRM once you're losing track of follow-ups or more than one person handles enquiries.

faq.q: Can I send marketing texts to my past customers?
faq.a: Only with their consent, and every message must identify your business and include an easy way to unsubscribe, under the Spam Act 2003.
